_about: Single source of truth for what the harness costs to enter. `targetBytes` is where the redesign is heading; measure-hotpath.mjs reports each route's bytes, ~tokens, and gap to target. Nothing here is enforced: size is information for the author, and the only failures are a missing declared file, an unbudgeted reference (drift), or an unusable budget.
_accounting: A route's cost is everything the doctrine MANDATES reading before the first line of work, not only what the platform loads by default. That includes the frontmatter of every skill (permanently in context as `available_skills`) and any reference a head skill requires unconditionally. Counting only the default-loaded files is the measurement trap that made the 23/08 rollback attack the wrong target: the corpus on disk fell 8% while the per-turn cost stayed flat.

_skillLimits: One kind of rule. `spec` rules come from the published Agent Skills specification and from anthropics/skills quick_validate.py, plus the two silent-trigger failures the platform does not report (unquoted colon in the description, H1 naming a dead skill). A violating skill can be rejected or never fire, so every violation is an error with no allowance. There are no size rules.
_driftCheck: The one structural failure of the meter. Every reference a head skill links to is either declared in the route that loads it, or listed under `onDemand` as consulted only inside a named branch. A link that appears in neither is drift: the doctrine grew a mandatory read that nobody measured. Missing declared files fail for the same reason; bytes never do.

onDemand.reason: Cursor migration at the delivered seal and reconciliation of the previous delivery. Fires at closeout and when opening a task on top of a delivered one — never between two tasks of the same plan.
The task reviewer briefing template — read by the coordinator when dispatching the per-task review, pasted into the reviewer prompt; never resident.
Dead-name sweep consulted only inside the Partial state remap branch — a consumer whose artifacts predate a harness skill rename; never resident.
